html:
Venezuela suffered hyperinflation from about 2016, when prices began rising faster than wages could follow. By 2018 prices were rising by over a million percent a year.

Oil prices crashed in 2014, and Venezuela, which earned nearly all its foreign money from oil, could not pay for imports. Price controls, seizures of businesses and mismanagement of the state oil company had already cut production. The government printed money to cover its spending. Shelves emptied, and people queued for hours for food and medicine.

The economy shrank by about three quarters, one of the deepest collapses in modern times outside war. Millions left in the Venezuelan refugee crisis. From 2019 the government let people use dollars, and inflation slowly fell. It was the end point of the oil state under Maduro.
sum: Venezuela suffered hyperinflation from about 2016, when prices began rising faster than wages could follow. By 2018 prices were rising by over a million percent a year.
